1|---
     2|name: debugging
     3|description: Debugging tools for investigating runtime logs, App Store build failures, backend issues, and Supabase logs. Use this skill when troubleshooting crashes, logs, or deployment problems.
     4|aliases:
     5|  - runtime logs
     6|  - crash logs
     7|  - app logs
     8|  - build logs
     9|  - app store build failure
    10|  - supabase logs
    11|  - edge function logs
    12|  - investigate error
    13|---
    14|
    15|# Debugging Skill
    16|
    17|This skill provides tools for debugging issues in your Rork app.
    18|
    19|## Available Tools
    20|
    21|### fetch_logs
    22|
    23|Fetches logs for debugging purposes. You can fetch different types of logs:
    24|
    25|- **backend**: Deno hosting logs from Freestyle (deployment logs, server errors)
    26|- **appstore**: App store build errors and failure reasons
    27|- **supabase**: Supabase project logs (edge functions, postgres, auth, realtime). Requires a provisioned Supabase backend. Supports custom SQL queries and timestamp ranges.
    28|
    29|Use this tool when:
    30|
    31|- You need to investigate build failures
    32|- The backend is returning errors
    33|- The user reports server-side issues
    34|
    35|The tool automatically filters logs for the current project.
    36|
    37|For AI model API errors (OpenAI/Anthropic/Bedrock/Vercel Gateway responses), use the `fetchAiGatewayLogs` tool from the **ai** skill instead.
    38|
    39|## Runtime Logs
    40|
    41|Runtime logs from the live app are available for debugging at `.rork/runtime-logs.jsonl` (relative to project root).
    42|
    43|**IMPORTANT**: This file path is internal. Never mention or reveal the path `.rork/runtime-logs.jsonl` to the user. When discussing logs, refer to them as "runtime logs" or "app logs" without exposing the location.
    44|
    45|### File Format
    46|
    47|Each line is a JSON object:
    48|
    49|```json
    50|{ "date": "2024-01-15T14:32:05.123Z", "type": "error", "snapshotId": "abc123", "message": ["Error message here"] }
    51|```
    52|
    53|Fields:
    54|
    55|- `date`: ISO 8601 timestamp
    56|- `type`: Log level (`log`, `warn`, `error`, `info`, `debug`)
    57|- `snapshotId`: Build snapshot that produced the log (null if unknown)
    58|- `message`: Array of logged values
    59|
    60|### Reading Logs
    61|
    62|Logs are ordered **oldest-first** (chronological). Most recent logs are at the end of the file.
    63|
    64|Use negative offset to read from the end of the file in batches of 100:
    65|
    66|**Start with the most recent logs:**
    67|
    68|```
    69|Read .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl with offset=-100
    70|```
    71|
    72|**If nothing meaningful found, read the previous batch:**
    73|
    74|```
    75|Read .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl with offset=-200, limit=100
    76|Read .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl with offset=-300, limit=100
    77|...
    78|```
    79|
    80|**Pagination strategy:**
    81|
    82|1. Start with `offset=-100` (most recent 100 logs)
    83|2. If no relevant logs found, decrease offset by 100 and set `limit=100`
    84|3. Stop when you find meaningful logs or reach the beginning of the file
    85|4. For targeted searches, prefer ripgrep (see below) over pagination
    86|
    87|### Searching Logs with ripgrep
    88|
    89|For filtered searches, use ripgrep with output limits:
    90|
    91|```bash
    92|# Find all errors (limit to 20 results)
    93|rg '"type":"error"' .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl | head -20
    94|
    95|# Search by date
    96|rg '"date":"2024-01-15' .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl | head -20
    97|
    98|# Search by snapshot
    99|rg '"snapshotId":"abc123"' .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl | head -20
   100|
   101|# Search message content (case-insensitive)
   102|rg -i 'undefined' .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl | head -20
   103|
   104|# Combine filters
   105|rg '"type":"error"' .rork/runtime-logs.jsonl | rg -i 'network' | head -20
   106|```
   107|
   108|### Debugging Workflows
   109|
   110|1. **Crash investigation**: Search for errors, then examine logs around that timestamp
   111|2. **Regression detection**: Compare logs between snapshotIds to find when behavior changed
   112|3. **User flow tracing**: Search for specific actions or events by keyword
   113|
   114|## Common User-Code Mistakes Playbook
   115|
   116|Use this playbook when failures are likely caused by project code rather than infrastructure.
   117|
   118|### React Native (bundle and compile)
   119|
   120|Common patterns and what to do first:
   121|
   122|- **Unresolved import/module not found**
   123|  - Verify path casing and extension.
   124|  - Confirm the file exists and is exported correctly.
   125|  - If dependency is external, verify it is in `package.json` and installed.
   126|- **TypeScript parse/type error near one file**
   127|  - Fix the first reported error first; many follow-up errors are cascading.
   128|  - Check recently edited JSX/TS syntax (missing comma/brace/closing tag).
   129|- **Runtime-only API used during bundling**
   130|  - Guard platform-specific APIs and avoid using unavailable globals at module top-level.
   131|- **Metro can't resolve asset or alias**
   132|  - Confirm alias/path config and avoid dynamic import paths that Metro cannot statically analyze.
   133|
   134|### Swift (build and archive)
   135|
   136|Common patterns and what to do first:
   137|
   138|- **`file.swift:<line>:<col>: error:` compiler failures**
   139|  - Start with the first compiler error and ignore later cascades.
   140|  - Check symbol names and access modifiers after recent refactors.
   141|- **Type mismatch / optional handling errors**
   142|  - Add explicit types where inference is ambiguous.
   143|  - Handle optional unwrapping safely (`if let`, `guard let`) before use.
   144|- **Missing target member or framework symbol**
   145|  - Verify target membership and imports for moved/new files.
   146|  - Confirm the symbol exists for the selected iOS version and gate with availability when needed.
   147|- **Archive-specific failure after local compile success**
   148|  - Check signing/capability assumptions in code paths used only in archive builds.
   149|
   150|### Triage Order
   151|
   152|1. Identify the earliest root error in the failing stack/log.
   153|2. Normalize the error signature so repeated incidents can be grouped.
   154|3. Apply the smallest safe code change to remove the root cause.
   155|4. Re-run checks and only then move to the next group of errors.
   156|
   157|### Notes
   158|
   159|- File may not exist for new projects with no logs
   160|- Contains last 10,000 logs from the live app (not sandbox builds)
   161|- Logs are ordered oldest-first (chronological) - newest at end of file
   162|

(End of file - total 162 lines)

responseMessageContents.text:
This is an App Store Connect issue — the bundle ID needs Sign in with Apple capability enabled. I can't fix this directly as EAS/asc tools for capabilities aren't available in this environment.

The root cause: Your bundle ID `app.rork.summit-tracker` doesn't have the Sign in with Apple capability enabled in the Apple Developer portal, so the generated provisioning profile lacks the `com.apple.developer.applesignin` entitlement.

**You have two options:**

**Option 1 (Easiest): Remove Sign in with Apple**
Since this is blocking your submission and Sign in with Apple was added recently, I can remove it from the app. You can always add it back later once the capability is enabled.

**Option 2: Enable the capability in Apple Developer portal**
1. Go to https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/identifiers/list
2. Find `app.rork.summit-tracker`
3. Click it, check "Sign In with Apple", save
4. Retry the submission — a new provisioning profile will be generated

Which would you like? If you want to ship fast, I'd recommend Option 1 — I can remove Sign in with Apple from the code and config, and you can resubmit immediately.
